why: Both moved the same single call site the same way with equivalent verification, so the decision rests on system-level judgment — and B's is deeper: six built, test-backed improvements against A's three, a dependency-aware ranking (cheap default gated on the vision fix and on surfacing errors, so a reasoning-budget-exhausted empty reply isn't silent), and three real app defects A never found (every exception swallowed so the bot silently ignores users, a new client plus leaked connection pool per Discord message on a 600s SDK timeout, and 'ollama' matching the 'llama' vision tag so local models were sent images they can't read). B also shows sharper Router-specific command — fallback_timeout as the actual stalled-stream guard that policy can't reach, a models list being incompatible with allow_flex_tier, BYOK Gemini costing a wasted 403 round trip under unlock_hosts, shadow models as the cheap way to validate the cheaper default on live traffic — where A's extra depth stops at Flex pricing it partly miscredits to routing itself.
A_best: The most faithful end-to-end proof: the real on_message driven with fake Discord objects through both the simulator and live Router, including the image path answering 'Red' to a red PNG, which validates the vision-tag change behaviourally rather than by table diff; its prompt-cache fix is also the more careful of the two, leaving a tag-free system prompt byte-identical (triple newlines included) by only collapsing blanks when clock lines are actually extracted.
B_best: Reading the app as a product rather than a call site: it ships the fix for the worst user-visible behaviour (silent failures), couples the cheap-model default to the two changes that make it safe, fixes the vision heuristic in both directions off the catalog, and builds fallbacks with a capability guard that drops text-only candidates on image requests — each with assertions that fail on the pre-change code.
A_worst: Thin improvement set relative to the app's real problems: the output cap and catalog-driven capabilities are only proposed, the silent-error and per-message-client defects are missed entirely, the vision fix is a new substring ('gpt-6') bolted onto the heuristic A itself calls a 2023-shaped guess, and the summary's 'routing alone also cuts the bill roughly in half' credits Router for an account-level Flex default, benchmarked against service_tier=default on Router rather than against the pre-migration OpenAI path.
B_worst: Two small correctness slips in shipped code: cacheable-prefix runs re.sub(r'\n{3,}') over every prompt, so a tag-free prompt with 3+ consecutive newlines is not 'sent exactly as it is today' as claimed, and catalog-vision reaches into the vendored runtime's private shape (CATALOG[id]['c']['in']), coupling app behaviour to a generated file's internals; its migration evidence also leans on a probe reproducing on_message rather than driving the handler itself, and its policy applies the cache key and timeout at defaults rather than scoped to the feature.
